title: From heart-rate data to training quantification: a comparison of 3 methods of training-intensity analysis
authors: Sylta O, Tonnessen E, Seiler S
journal: International Journal of Sports Physiology and Performance
population: Elite cross-country skiers (16 male, 13 female; VO2max 76 +/- 7), about 14-day altitude camp
findings: 570 sessions analysed by time in zone (TIZ), session goal (SG) and a hybrid SG/TIZ method.
TIZ and SG/TIZ put 96.1% and 95.5% of total time in zone 1, with 2.9%/3.6% in zone 2 and 1.1%/0.8% in zone 3.
Counting sessions by goal (SG) gave 86.6% zone 1 sessions and 11.1% / 2.4% zone 2 / zone 3.
Conversion factors TIZ or SG/TIZ to SG and back were 0.9 / 1.1 in zone 1 and 3.0 / 0.33 in zones 2-3.
limitations: Skiers at a camp, HR-based zones only; factors depend on session structure and are not validated for runners or pace-based zones.
implications: Compute TID both ways, time-in-zone and session-goal, because the same training reads about 96% vs about 87% zone 1.

When comparing a plan with a literature target such as 80/20, state which counting method the target uses; an 80/20 split by session count implies far more than 80% of time in zone 1 (in this sample).
Store a planned zone per session so both views can be derived.

verification.notes: Crossref matches (Jan 2014). Result figures read from PubMed efetch (Europe PMC truncated at '<'). P-values omitted.
